page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 architecture processors running at 3.9 GHz. The hardware provides 96 physical cores presenting 192 virtual CPUs with multithreading enabled. The system features 1536.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core. Because this is a bare-metal deployment, operating systems and hypervisors run directly on the physical hardware without hypervisor latency or virtualization overhead.

The server does not include integrated local solid-state or magnetic storage devices, requiring all persistent file systems and boot partitions to utilize remote network-attached volumes. Graphics accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on the platform. To support high-capacity interconnects and remote storage throughput, the platform includes a baseline network interface capacity of 200 Gbps.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, bare-metal deployment eliminates virtualization resource overhead, allowing full exploitation of the 192 processing threads and 1.5 TB memory array. The absence of local disk requires planning for network storage consumption across the 200 Gbps link. The r8ib.metal-48xl is designed for enterprise memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale in-memory databases, distributed memory caching nodes, memory-bound enterprise resource management, and high-throughput real-time analytical processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r8ib.metal-48xl is a bare-metal memory-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors running at 3.9 GHz. It features 96 physical cores, 192 virtual CPUs, and 1536.0 GB of system memory, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio without hypervisor virtualization overhead. The server is not provisioned with local physical storage drives, requiring external network-attached storage architectures, and does not contain discrete GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a 200 Gbps baseline interface, delivering substantial bandwidth for cluster communication and storage transfer operations. The large memory pool and dedicated high-frequency core count make this platform cost-efficient for maximizing density in non-virtualized enterprise environments. The r8ib.metal-48xl is structured for workloads such as large in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale ETL operations, and memory-bound transactional data processing.
